name: Dún Aonghusa

attributes.attribute: stone fort on Inis Mór in the Aran Islands
stands on a cliff 87 meters above Galway Bay
uses a sheer cliff as protection on one side
band of upright stones hindering access to the inner fort
legendary builders who named the fort for Angus

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dún Aonghusa is a stone fort on Inis Mór, the largest of the Aran Islands. It sits on a cliff about 87 meters above Galway Bay. A sheer cliff protects one side; stone walls protect the rest. The fort has an inner stone enclosure and two outer walls. Fragments of a third wall survive. A band of upright stones, called a chevaux-de-frise, blocks access to the inner fort. The outermost defences enclose about 5.7 hectares. Dry-stone ramparts without mortar form the walls. The innermost wall survives to 4.9 meters high and over 5 meters thick. Legend says the Fir Bolg, the second mythological race in Ireland, built the fort and named it for their chief Angus.

okr.objective: Document Dún Aonghusa, the great stone fort of Inis Mór.
key_results: Locate the fort and its cliff top on Inis Mór in the Aran Islands.
